scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree listening to a gesturing follower. Behind them, robed Pharisees converse while a disciple baptizes a person in the river and others gather nearby; golden hills and a village rise in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 4:1, in which Jesus learns that the Pharisees have heard he is making and baptizing more disciples than John. The setting and conversations are imagined; the disciple performing the baptism reflects the clarification in John 4:2.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands on a riverbank while two disciples baptize a man and a woman in the water, with hills and a village beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative riverside scene illustrating John 4:2: Jesus himself did not baptize; his disciples did. The setting and the participants' appearances are imagined. The chapter identifies its English word glosses as Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a winding country path away from a stone settlement, with hills and water in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus' journey: John 4:3 says he left Judea and went again into Galilee. The setting and details are artistic interpretation. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a rocky path through sunlit hills, with olive trees, stone terraces, and a village in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus passing through Samaria in John 4:4. The landscape and visual details are artistic interpretation. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks toward a stone town beside a cultivated field bordered by low stone walls and olive trees, with sunlit hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:5: Jesus comes to Sychar in Samaria near the plot of ground Jacob gave his son Joseph. The town and landscape are artistic interpretations. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus rests wearily on the edge of a stone well, his head in his hand, as a sunlit path winds through fields and hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 4:6: Jesus, weary from his journey, sits at Jacob's well about the sixth hour. His appearance and the well and landscape are artistic interpretation. The scene follows the verse and its Berean Interlinear token glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman holding a clay jar stands beside a stone well and looks toward Jesus, who is seated and gestures to her. A rope hangs from a wooden crossbeam, with trees, hills, and a village in the sunlit background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:7, where a woman from Samaria comes to draw water and Jesus asks her for a drink. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A group of robed travelers in a sunlit stone-town market, one offering coins to a seller holding flatbreads, with baskets of fruit and other food on the stall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus' disciples in the city to buy food, as John 4:8 describes. The market, people, and exchange are artistic details; the verse's token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A Samaritan woman gestures in surprise toward Jesus, who sits beside a stone well; her clay water jar stands at her side in a sunny landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:9: the Samaritan woman questions Jesus about his request for a drink, and the verse notes that Jews did not associate with Samaritans. The setting and gestures are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on the edge of a stone well and speaks with an open hand to a Samaritan woman standing beside a large clay water jar. Water glints in the well, with trees, hills, and a village in the sunlit distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 4:10, where Jesus speaks of the gift of God and says that the woman would have asked him and he would have given her living water. The visible water and setting are artistic choices. The source verse's English token glosses are Berean Interlinear glosses marked uncurated, not GBT-approved.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures toward a deep stone well as she speaks to Jesus, who sits beside it with empty hands; an earthen jar rests near her.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined moment inspired by John 4:11: the woman asks Jesus where He has living water when He has nothing to draw with and the well is deep. The word glosses used to guide the scene are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, as identified in the reader's source note.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman holding a clay jar gestures toward Jesus, who sits beside a stone well. Sheep and a cow drink at a trough behind them in a sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of the Samaritan woman asking Jesus whether he is greater than Jacob, who gave the well and from which he, his sons, and his livestock drank. The animals evoke her reference; the verse does not say they were present during the conversation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as he speaks to the Samaritan woman beside a stone well; a clay water jar and cup sit nearby in a sunlit, dry landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at the well as he says that everyone who drinks this water will thirst again. The setting and visual details are artistic interpretation; the token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a woman seated beside a stone well, her clay water jar nearby, while a ribbon of water and flowering greenery rises from her chest into the sunlit air.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene visualizes Jesus' promise that the water he gives becomes a spring within the recipient, welling up to eternal life. The visible spring and flowers are an artistic metaphor, not a visible event described in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman extends her open hands toward Jesus, who sits beside a round stone well. A clay water jar and rope rest nearby in a sunlit, hilly landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates the woman asking Jesus for water so that she will not thirst or need to come here to draw, in John 4:15. The appearance, gestures, and landscape are artistic interpretation. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well and gestures toward a distant village while the Samaritan woman stands beside a clay water jar and listens.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the conversation at the well as Jesus tells the woman to go, call her husband, and come here, following the verse's Berean Interlinear token glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman stands beside a clay jar with one hand on her chest, speaking with Jesus, who sits by a stone well and gestures gently. Sunlit hills and a distant village fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:17, where the woman answers that she has no husband and Jesus says she has spoken correctly. The setting, expressions, and gestures are artistic choices; the verse relationship follows the Berean Interlinear token glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well, speaking with a woman holding a clay water jar. Five pebbles together and one apart rest on the well in a sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes Jesus' conversation with the Samaritan woman in John 4:18, where he acknowledges that she has spoken truthfully and speaks of her five past husbands and the man who is not her husband now. The pebbles are an artistic addition suggesting those relationships.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures as she speaks to Jesus, who sits beside a stone well. A clay water jar rests nearby, with a leafy tree, sunlit hills and a village around them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John 4:19, in which the woman tells Jesus she understands him to be a prophet. The well comes from the surrounding passage; the lesson identifies its English token glosses as Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A Samaritan woman gestures toward a mountain while speaking with Jesus beside a stone well; a water jar and a winding road sit among sunlit hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the conversation in John 4:20, where the woman contrasts her ancestors' worship on the mountain with the claim that Jerusalem is the place to worship. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a sunlit mountain while speaking with a woman beside a stone well; her clay water jar rests at her feet.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene portrays Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman as he tells her that a time is coming when worship of the Father will be neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. The setting and gestures are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well, speaking with an open hand to a Samaritan woman seated near a clay water jar, with sunlit hills and olive trees behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well. In John 4:22 he contrasts worship of what is not known with worship of what is known and says that salvation is from the Jews. The chapter's word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor illustration of Jesus seated by a stone well speaking with a Samaritan woman beside a clay jar, with people praying in the sunlit fields beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at the well. The distant worshipers are an artistic addition illustrating John 4:23, where Jesus speaks of true worshipers worshiping the Father in spirit and truth and says that the Father seeks such worshipers.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well, one hand over his heart and the other raised toward the sky, while a Samaritan woman listens beside a clay water jar. A sunlit village and hills lie in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places Jesus and the Samaritan woman at the well as he teaches that God is Spirit and that worship must be in spirit and truth. The gestures and setting interpret the teaching rather than depicting details stated in this verse. The chapter's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures toward Jesus beside a stone well, with a clay water jar in the foreground and sunlit hills and a village behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:25, where the woman speaks of the coming Messiah, called Christ, who will tell them all things. The appearance and details of the scene are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits at a stone well and gestures as he speaks to a Samaritan woman beside her clay water jar, with sunlit trees and hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:26 and its setting at Jacob's well: Jesus speaks to the Samaritan woman after she mentions the coming Messiah. The source identifies the English word glosses as Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well and speaks with a woman next to a clay water jar, while four arriving disciples look on in surprise in a sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:27: Jesus speaks with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well as his disciples arrive, amazed but not voicing the questions mentioned in the verse. The scene is informed by the Berean Interlinear token glosses; the appearances and setting details are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures while speaking to two men near a stone town gate; a clay water pot stands unattended beside a well behind her.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of John 4:28: the woman leaves her water pot, goes into the city, and speaks to the men. The setting, appearance, and gestures are artistic interpretation. The word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear Bible and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman gestures to attentive townspeople in a sunlit stone village, inviting them toward a man seated beside a distant well.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows the Samaritan woman inviting the townspeople to see the man who told her what she had done and asking whether he could be the Christ, as in John 4:29. The appearances, setting, and gestures are imagined. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Townspeople walk out of a stone city along a sunlit path toward Jesus, who sits beside a well under a tree.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:30, in which people go out of the city and come to Jesus; the figures and setting are artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well while a disciple offers him bread and other disciples gather around beneath a tree.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the disciples asking Jesus, their Rabbi, to eat in John 4:31. The bread, gestures and visual details are imagined; the well follows the surrounding passage. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well and gestures as he speaks to four disciples. One holds a basket of bread, while the others listen beneath a leafy tree in a sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene depicts Jesus telling his disciples that he has food to eat which they do not know, as reflected in the Berean Interlinear token glosses. The offered bread evokes their earlier invitation to eat; the food he speaks of is left unpictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beside a stone well as four disciples turn toward one another with puzzled expressions and questioning gestures. Trees, fields, hills, and a distant village fill the sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 4:33, where the disciples ask one another whether someone brought Jesus anything to eat. The well comes from the surrounding passage; the figures' appearances and gestures are imagined. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to attentive disciples beside a stone well. One holds a basket of bread as villagers approach from a sunlit town.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 4:34, where Jesus describes His food as doing the will of the One who sent Him and finishing His work. The bread and approaching villagers suggest the surrounding story; their appearance and arrangement are imagined. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a sunlit field of pale ripe grain while a group of listeners gathers around him, with hills and a village in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene draws on John 4:35 and its Berean Interlinear token glosses: Jesus asks his listeners to lift their eyes and see fields already white for harvest. The setting and figures are an artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two smiling field workers in robes face each other in a golden field. One scatters seed, while the other carries a basket and armful of grain, with a small pouch at his belt.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene echoes the harvest metaphor in John 4:36: the sower and reaper rejoice together, while the reaper gathers the harvest and a small pouch suggests the reward. The abundant field and warm light allude to fruit for eternal life.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit countryside, one farmer scatters seeds over dark tilled soil while another cuts ripe golden grain with a sickle.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of the saying in John 4:37: one person sows and another reaps.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a golden wheat field as disciples look on; reapers cut and gather grain while other workers labor among sheaves in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates Jesus sending his followers to reap where others have already labored, as described in John 4:38.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A Samaritan woman gestures as she speaks to attentive townspeople outside a sunlit stone city, while Jesus sits by a stone well in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 4:39, where many Samaritans believe in Jesus because of the woman's testimony that he told her all she had done. The setting and gestures are artistic interpretation. The verse's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks with smiling Samaritan villagers as a man gestures toward the open doorway of a stone home, with hills and village houses beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative welcome illustrates the Samaritans asking Jesus to stay with them in John 4:40. The verse says he stayed there two days; this single scene does not depict the duration.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as he speaks to a gathering of Samaritan villagers beneath a leafy tree, while more people approach along a path between sunlit stone houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Samaritan villagers hearing Jesus in the setting of John 4:41, where many more believed because of his word; the English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone village courtyard, Samaritan townspeople speak animatedly with a woman in a head covering, while a seated man gestures toward Jesus standing beside them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates John 4:42, where the Samaritans tell the woman that they have heard for themselves and know Jesus is truly the Savior of the world. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, wearing light robes, walks along a sunlit path away from a village, with people behind him and fields, hills, and a lake in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 4:43 says that after two days he departed from there for Galilee; the preceding passage places him among the Samaritans. This scene imagines the village, figures, and journey.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures while speaking to three men beneath a tree near a sunlit hillside village; a woman with a jar and a man working attend to their tasks beside the stone houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene illustrates Jesus’ testimony that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. The setting, companions, and townspeople’s actions are artistic interpretations, not details stated in John 4:44.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, wearing a cream tunic and reddish-brown mantle, is warmly greeted by Galilean men and women on a sunlit stone path. Olive branches, village houses, hills, and a glimpse of water fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined welcome in Galilee illustrates John 4:45: the Galileans received Jesus after seeing what he had done in Jerusalem during the feast, which they themselves had attended. The meeting and its setting are artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A concerned royal official sits beside his sick son, resting a hand on the boy's head as he lies in bed. A lakeside village is visible through the window.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the royal official and his sick son in Capernaum mentioned in John 4:46. The verse also says Jesus returned to Cana of Galilee, where he had made water into wine.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus listens as a worried man in ornate blue robes gestures down a sunlit village road, with a lake and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 4:47: a royal official asks Jesus to come down and heal his son, who is near death. The setting and gestures are imagined; the son is not shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand to a richly dressed royal official while several people listen in a sunlit village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Jesus speaking to the royal official in John 4:48 about seeing signs and wonders and believing. The listeners, setting, and appearances are imagined. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, keyed to the Nestle 1904 Greek text by biblicalhumanities.org; they are not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A richly dressed royal official kneels with outstretched hands as Jesus listens beneath a tree; a winding road crosses the sunlit hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 4:49, in which the royal official asks Jesus to come down before his child dies. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit village road, Jesus extends his hand toward a man who looks back at him while walking away with a staff and a bundle.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 4:50: Jesus tells the man to go because his son lives; the man believes Jesus' word and goes on his way. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two servants meet a robed father on a sunlit road; one gestures as the father listens, with hills, trees, and a distant village behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined meeting based on John 4:51 and the Berean Interlinear word glosses: as the father goes down, his servants meet him with the news that his boy lives. The setting, clothing, and expressions are artistic details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit road above a lake, a richly robed father listens as a servant gestures while two other servants stand nearby.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene shows the father asking his servants when his son began to get better. In John 4:52, they answer that the fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour. The landscape and gestures are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded father holds his smiling son's hand at his bedside, looking upward as five members of the household gather in a warm, sunlit home.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 4:53: the father recognized that the hour matched Jesus' words that his son lived, and he and his whole household believed. The home, gathering, gestures, and appearances are artistic choices. The English token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus, in a white robe and red cloak, speaks to a richly dressed royal official on a sunlit stone path in a Galilean village, with blue water and hills in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene recalls Jesus reassuring the royal official in Cana. John 4:54 identifies the healing of the official's son at a distance as Jesus' second sign after coming from Judea to Galilee.
